verdict.summary: Supermicro is the batch’s purest rack-scale AI revenue accelerator and one of its weakest quality translations. Preliminary FY2026 revenue reached $39.1B, up from $22.0B, but GAAP gross margin was only 10.8% for the year even after Q4 recovered to 17.5%. Cash of $7.5B sits against $8.7B of debt and convertible obligations. The August earnings 8-K reports $1.407B net proceeds from common issuance and $4.231B from mandatory-convertible preferred issuance, confirming that both June transactions executed; the separate $1.25B ATM remains capacity without evidenced sales. The 59/100 score reflects explosive demand offset by thin economics, control risk and a materially expanded denominator. FY2027 revenue guidance of $65B-$72B is powerful but preliminary, and management warned that an export-control review could affect forecasts or prior amounts. The lifecycle remains wait and the preserved levels remain dormant until fresh regular-session geometry is captured. Wait: SMCI's old $38.95 framework is dormant while the enlarged common and preferred claims reset the denominator. Require fresh RTH price and volume structure before defining activation or size.

business.overview:
Supermicro designs modular servers, storage, networking and full rack-scale systems. Revenue is driven by unit volume, GPU and accelerator content, average rack value, customer acceptance timing and the speed with which component purchases become delivered systems. The company competes on fast platform qualification, liquid cooling, dense integration and deployment rather than on ownership of the underlying accelerators.

The AI transmission channel is direct: NVIDIA and other accelerator shipments create demand for Supermicro’s servers, power distribution, cooling, networking and rack integration. Q4 FY2026 sales of $11.1B and FY2027 revenue guidance of $65B-$72B imply very large cluster deployments, but component pass-through can inflate revenue without equivalent gross profit. Working capital and supply commitments can therefore grow faster than earnings.

What breaks is conversion quality. Customer concentration, GPU allocation, acceptance delays, export restrictions or a shift toward hyperscaler-designed racks can strand inventory and compress margins. The August earnings exhibit reports net proceeds matching full exercise of both the 6.818M common-share option and the 11.25M depositary-share option; the completed common and mandatory-convertible financings must therefore be included, while the $1.25B ATM remains unsold capacity. The export-control review and prior material-weakness language require controls and financing claims to remain separate from genuine AI demand.
business.moat: Supermicro’s moat is speed: modular building blocks, liquid-cooling engineering and rack-level integration shorten deployment cycles for rapidly changing accelerators. It is weaker than a proprietary-chip moat because customers can dual-source systems and pass-through hardware limits pricing power.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: SMCI reported 601,377,832 common shares before the June financing. The August earnings exhibit records $1.406753B net common-issuance proceeds, matching the prospectus's full-option case and proving 45,454,545 base shares plus the 6,818,181-share option, or 653,650,558 legal common shares after the deal. It also records $4.230844B net mandatory-convertible proceeds, matching full exercise of the 11.25M-depositary-share option. The resulting 86.25M depositary shares carry a $4.3125B liquidation claim and convert into approximately 130.686M-156.820M common shares, subject to adjustments. Q4 basic and diluted weighted-average shares were 613.484M and 705.001M because issuance occurred during the quarter; Q1 FY2027 guidance assumes 745M GAAP and 761M non-GAAP diluted shares. The separate $1.25B ATM remains capacity without evidenced sales, so no single current fully diluted point-in-time total is asserted.

filingsReview.summary: 9 decision-relevant primary filing(s) are displayed with accession-specific findings. Grade C+ measures fundamentals; trade state wait measures timing and is evaluated separately.

filings.finding: The Q3 FY2026 Form 10-Q reports 601,377,832 shares outstanding and reconciles 600.205M basic weighted-average shares to 692.189M diluted through 73.803M convertible-note and 18.181M other security shares; another 60.791M potential shares were anti-dilutive and excluded.

The June 9 Form S-3ASR is an automatic shelf registration covering potential future securities offerings. It establishes registration capacity only and provides no evidence of common shares delivered, ATM sales, preferred conversion, debt proceeds or completed financing.

The FY2025 Form 10-K provides the audited capital and control baseline, including material-weakness disclosures; it is the comparison point for evaluating whether subsequent remediation and accelerated fiscal 2026 growth are reliable.

The August 11 Form 8-K furnishes preliminary Q4 and FY2026 results. Its $1.406753B net common proceeds and $4.230844B net mandatory-convertible proceeds match the full-option cases in the prospectuses, proving exercise of both options; Q4 basic/diluted weighted-average shares were 613.484M/705.001M and Q1 guidance assumes 745M/761M diluted shares. It does not prove ATM sales.

The June 11 final Form 424B5 establishes an up-to-$1.25B at-the-market common-stock program. It is primary equity capacity, not straight debt, mandatory-convertible preferred or a secondary resale, and it does not prove that any specified amount was sold.

The June 12 final Form 424B5 covers 75M depositary shares plus an 11.25M option, each representing 1/20 of the 7.00% Series A mandatory-convertible preferred. The August proceeds prove full exercise, creating a $4.3125B liquidation claim and approximately 130.686M-156.820M common equivalents; it is equity-linked financing, not an ATM.

The final Form 424B5 prices 45,454,545 primary common shares plus a 6,818,181-share underwriter option. The August $1.406753B net-proceeds disclosure matches the full-option case, proving 52,272,726 completed shares and a 653,650,558 post-deal legal common denominator.

This preliminary Form 424B5 describes the 75M-depositary-share base deal and approximately 113.64M-136.37M base conversion equivalents. The final prospectus and August proceeds supersede that base case by proving the 11.25M option was exercised, raising the range to about 130.686M-156.820M.

This preliminary Form 424B5 describes the common-stock offering of 45,454,545 shares and the 6,818,181-share option; the instrument is primary common equity, not warrants, debt or a secondary-only registration.
